title: Production of recombinant hBD-1 in _Escherichia coli_ and its specific polyclonal antibody in rabbits
protocol: Transform protease-deficient E. coli BL21(DE3)pLysS strain with the pET32a-hBD-1 expression vector as described.
Spread transformation on LB medium plates containing carbenicillin (50 µg/ml) and chloramphenicol (34 µg/ml).
Incubate the plates overnight at 37°C.
Inoculate 3 ml of TSB medium containing carbenicillin (50 µg/ml) and chloramphenicol (34 µg/ml) with a single-drug-resistant colony of E. coli cells.
Grow overnight culture at 37°C with shaking.
Inoculate 3 ml of fresh TSB medium containing carbenicillin (50 µg/ml) and chloramphenicol (34 µg/ml) with 10 µl of overnight culture.
Grow the culture until absorbance at 600 nm reaches 0.4-0.6 at 37°C with shaking.
Transfer the culture to three Eppendorf tubes and centrifuge at 3,000 x g for 1 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in TSB medium containing carbenicillin (50 µg/ml), chloramphenicol (34 µg/ml) and 15% glycerol.
Vortex the vial vigorously to ensure even mixing of bacterial culture and glycerol.
Aliquot 200 µl into labeled 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes.
Freeze at -80°C.
Use stock culture to inoculate 50 ml of LB medium in 250 ml flask and grow overnight at 37°C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Make a 1:50 dilution of 4 ml of the saturated overnight culture in 196 ml fresh M9 medium containing carbenicillin (50 µg/ml) and chloramphenicol (34 µg/ml) in a 1-l flask.
Grow cells at 37°C with shaking at 200 rpm to mid-log phase (the absorbance at 600 nm reaches approximately 0.6).
Add IPTG (1 mM final concentration) and sterile glucose (0.4 g per 200 ml culture). Incubate for an additional 4 h at 37°C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Centrifuge the cell culture at 6000 x g for 5 min at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Suspend the cell pellet in a 50-ml centrifuge tube by adding 5 ml of 1×LEW buffer containing 0.5 mM EDTA per 300 ml of culture and freeze at -80°C.
Thaw cells at room temperature for at most 20 min and keep the sample on ice.
Sonicate on ice for short bursts (5 second burst and 10 second rest, repeat 8 times).
Centrifuge at 13500 x g for 45 min at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant.
Pour the supernatant through a 0.45-μm filter.
Collect the filtrate.
Add calcium chloride to a final concentration of 10 mM before chromatography.
Apply the supernatant to a HisTrapTM HP-prepared column equilibrated in 20 mM sodium phosphate buffer \(pH 7.4) and 500 mM sodium chloride.
Wash the column with the buffer until a stable baseline is reached.
Elute the fusion protein with a linear gradient over 12 column volumes into 20 mM sodium phosphate buffer \(pH 7.4), 500 mM sodium chloride, and 500 mM imidazole.
Identify fractions containing the fusion protein by SDS-PAGE analysis, MALDI-MS, or ESI-QTOF-MS if necessary.
Pool the fractions containing the fusion protein.
Concentrate the pooled fractions with an Amicon 3-kDa membrane.
Dialyze against 1 x PBS.
Collect the sample.
Adjust the sample to a concentration of 7.5 mg/ml.
Perform quick dilution to 0.2 mg/ml with refolding buffer containing 100 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.5, 1 mM EDTA, 1.5 M urea, 0.3 mM GSSG and 3.0 mM GSH.
Gently swirl to mix.
Incubate at room temperature for 30 min.
Perform a further dilution to a concentration of 0.1 mg/ml with the same volume of refolding buffer containing 100 mM Tris/HCl, pH 8.5, 1 mM EDTA, 1.5 M urea, 5.7 mM GSSG and 3.0 mM GSH.
Incubate for 16 h with shaking at 50 rpm at room temperature.
Concentrate the protein solution using an Amicon 3-kD membrane.
Dialyze against enterokinase buffer (50 mM Tris/HCl, pH 8.0, 1 mM CaCl2).
Adjust the dialyzed pET32a-hBD-1 protein solution to a final concentration of 0.5 mg/ml and add 0.1% (v/v) Tween-20.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight with enterokinase (1 U per 250 μg of fusion proteins).
Pour the digestion mixture through a 0.45-μm filter and collect the filtrate.
Load the filtrate onto an FPLC MonoS HR5/5 column equilibrated with 20 mM Tris/HCl (pH 8.2).
Elute hBD-1 protein using a linear gradient over 10 column volumes into 20 mM Tris-HCl buffer (pH 8.2) containing 1.0 M sodium chloride.
Identify fractions containing the hBD-1 protein by ESI-QTOF-MS analysis.
Pool the peak fractions containing hBD-1.
Adjust the pH value to 3-4 with 5% TFA.
Apply the solution to a Jupiter C18 column for purification.
Identify fractions containing the oxidized, correctly folded hBD-1 protein by SDS-PAGE and ESI-QTOF-MS analysis.
Pool the peak fractions containing the desired hBD-1.
Lyophilize until dry.
Store the oxidized hBD-1 at −20 °C.
Dissolve the lyophilized oxidized hBD-1 in 50 mM NH4HCO3 buffer (pH 8.0).
Add 20 mM DTT and incubate at 37 °C for 2 hours in the dark, or alternatively,
Dissolve the lyophilized oxidized hBD-1 in 0.1% TFA.
Add 20 mM Tris-Carboxethyl-Phosphin (TCEP) and incubate at room temperature for 2 hours.
Further purify reduced hBD-1 by high resolution RP-HPLC as STEP-32.
Identify fractions containing the desired protein by ESI-QTOF-MS analysis.
Dissolve lyophilized, reduced hBD-1 in 50 mM NH4HCO3 buffer (pH 8.0).
Add iodoacetamide (IAA) to the dissolved hBD-1 to achieve a final concentration of 50 mM.
Incubate the alkylated hBD-1 at 37 °C in the dark for 1 hour.
Purify the alkylated hBD-1 by RP-HPLC C2C18 using the same system as described above.
Dilute 4 mg KLH in 4 ml PBS and add 4 μl of fresh 25% glutaraldehyde.
Mix well the diluted KLH and incubate at 100 rpm at room temperature for 1 hour.
Transfer the mixture to four 30-kD vivaspins and centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 10 minutes.
Wash with 500 μl PBS and centrifuge again at 12,000 x g.
Repeat the washing step two more times.
Dilute the washed mixture with 1.6 ml PBS to get a final concentration of 2.5 mg/ml.
Mix well the protein mixture (HPLC-purified carboxamidomethylated hBD-1 and reduced hBD-1) and the glutaraldehyde-treated KLH solution.
Incubate the mixed solution at 100 rpm at room temperature for 1 hour.
Use a pH below the pI of Lysine for the reaction.
Stop the reaction with 20 μl of 1 M Tris-HCl (pH8.0).
Dilute the stopped reaction with PBS to make a solution containing 0.2-0.3 mg/ml peptide.
Store the diluted solution in aliquots at −20 °C until further use.
Immunize rabbits with 300 μg KLH-conjugated peptides initially.
Boost immunization in each rabbit with 200 μg KLH-conjugated peptides after 2, 4, and 7 weeks respectively.
Bleed the rabbits 2 weeks after the last booster injection.
Collect supernatant (serum) from the treated blood and filter it with a 0.22 µm filter.
Store the filtered serum in aliquots at −80 °C until further use.
Apply the serum to a HiTrap™ Protein G HP column (GE Healthcare) for IgG separation.
Return the pH of each eluate immediately to neutral pH.
Prepare two affinity columns using 1 mg of highly purified alkylated hBD-1 covalently bound to a HiTrap NHS activated HP 1 ml column.
Purify polyclonal antibodies from Protein G-purified IgG fractions by affinity chromatography.
Return the pH of each elutate immediately to neutral pH after purification.
Apply purified IgG-fraction to the affinity column containing oxidized hBD-1 to deplete cross-reacting antibodies.
Test the effluent for specificity using immuno-dot blot analyses and western blot analyses with correctly folded, oxidized hBD-1, fully reduced hBD-1, and alkylated hBD-1.
Transfer the linearized hBD-1-recognizing antibody solution in the flow-through to an Amicon Ultra-50 (Millipore).
Concentrate the antibody solution by centrifugation.
Dilute the concentrated antibody solution in PBS.
Return the pH of each eluate immediately to a neutral pH.
Store the concentrated and diluted antibody solution in aliquots at -80°C.
